verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs"),path=require("path");const fail=(m)=>{console.error(m);process.exit(1)};const read=(f)=>fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8");const walk=(d)=>{if(!fs.existsSync(d))return[];return fs.readdirSync(d,{withFileTypes:true}).flatMap((x)=>{const p=path.join(d,x.name);return x.isDirectory()?(x.name==="node_modules"?[]:walk(p)):[p]})};const v1=()=>walk("app/api/v1").filter((f)=>/route\.ts$/.test(f));const v1src=()=>v1().map(read).join("\n");const f=v1().filter((x)=>/@\/lib\/core\/(load-capabilities|capabilities)/.test(read(x)));if(!f.length)fail("no /api/v1 endpoint projects the capability resolver to a client, so a native app cannot know which actions to show");console.log("ok")'

append.detail: 2026-10-06: GET /api/v1/capabilities?kind=&id= projects the web's capability loaders (lib/core/load-capabilities, and the Space role as space.* names) to a client; display only, every write re-checks. Bearer callers reach lib code through asCaller, which binds the verified token so createClient() and getCachedUser() answer as that caller under RLS (lib/supabase/request-identity.ts); view-as never applies there. Tested in app/api/v1/capabilities/route.test.ts and lib/supabase/request-identity.test.ts.
